name: Tbilisi
tagline: Ultra-Affordable European Capital with 8,000 Years of Wine and Warmth
description: Tbilisi is the FIRE world's best-kept secret — a stunningly affordable European capital where ancient sulfur baths, 8,000-year-old wine traditions, and jaw-dropping Caucasus mountain scenery come at a fraction of the cost of anywhere in Western Europe. Georgia's digital nomad-friendly visa policies, zero tax on foreign income for most residents, legendary hospitality, and a food scene that rivals any Mediterranean city make Tbilisi arguably the highest-value FIRE destination on the planet.

quickFacts.visa: 1-year visa-free stay for most nationalities. Remotely from Georgia program for digital workers. Easy residency permits via business registration or property ownership.
quickFacts.timezone: UTC+4 (Georgia Standard Time, no daylight saving)
quickFacts.language: Georgian (English growing among younger population, Russian also common)
quickFacts.internetSpeed: 40-150 Mbps (fiber expanding rapidly, excellent café Wi-Fi)
quickFacts.safetyRating: Very Safe — extremely low violent crime, one of the safest capitals in Europe, very welcoming to foreigners
quickFacts.nearestAirport: Tbilisi International Airport Shota Rustaveli (TBS) — 20 min from city center
quickFacts.climate: Continental with cold winters (0-5°C) and hot summers (28-35°C). Beautiful spring and autumn seasons, moderate rainfall year-round.

housing.description: Characterful small studio in Old Tbilisi/Sololaki/Marjanishvili, or a modern studio in Saburtalo; older fit-out, walkable streets

dining.description: Mostly home cooking with regular cheap local meals (khachapuri, khinkali, a bakery lunch)

healthcare.description: Basic local insurance plan plus out-of-pocket clinic visits (GP $15–30)

transportation.description: Metromoney metro/bus pass plus occasional Bolt rides

entertainment.description: A budget gym plus occasional cinema and casual outings

1M.lifestyle: Tbilisi at the lean end is one of the most affordable footholds in the whole tool, and the base is already so low that housing and healthcare form a floor that cannot compress much further. A charming central studio, cheap and frequent local food, and one of Europe's cheapest transit systems make daily life genuinely comfortable rather than merely survivable. The trade-offs are real: winter heating bills spike, some buildings are dated, English thins out quickly outside younger and expat circles, and complex healthcare may mean traveling. For a frugal, walkable, café-and-market lifestyle, this tier delivers a lot.

housing.description: Nice renovated 1BR in a desirable central area (Vera, the Vake edge, or near Mtatsminda)

dining.description: Regular dining out mixing cheap local spots with mid-range restaurants

healthcare.description: A better local private plan with wider clinic access

transportation.description: Bolt-first daily travel with transit as backup

entertainment.description: A quality gym plus more frequent cultural and social outings

2M.lifestyle: This tier moves into a properly comfortable rhythm: a renovated one-bedroom in a leafy, walkable district, dining out several times a week, and Bolt on demand instead of waiting for a bus. Central Tbilisi's café culture, wine bars, and sulphur-bath quarter are all within easy reach. The city's rougher infrastructure — patchy pavements, older plumbing, seasonal utility swings — is still present but easily absorbed at this budget. It is an easy, low-friction European-adjacent lifestyle at a fraction of EU prices.

housing.description: Premium 1BR or small 2BR in a top area (Vake, or a renovated flat in Old Tbilisi)

dining.description: Frequent mid-range dining with occasional higher-end meals

healthcare.description: Comprehensive local private plan / MediClub Georgia membership, English-speaking clinics

entertainment.description: Premium gym plus regular concerts, dining-out socialising, and events

3M.lifestyle: The FIRE tier buys a premium address in Vake or a beautifully renovated Old Tbilisi flat, with the freedom to eat out often, keep a good gym, and treat ride-hailing as the default. Healthcare steps up to a comprehensive local plan or a MediClub membership with English-speaking doctors — reassuring, though the country's most complex care is still better handled abroad in Istanbul or Vienna. This is an unmistakably comfortable European-city lifestyle that lands far below what the same quality costs in Berlin or western Iberia.

housing.description: High-spec apartment or small villa in a prime area (Vake, or the Tskneti/Kojori hills)

dining.description: Frequent dining at the city's best restaurants, including regular fine dining

healthcare.description: International/regional insurance plan with cross-border cover

transportation.description: A private car (owned/leased) plus ride-hailing for convenience

entertainment.description: Club memberships, cultural events, weekend Caucasus trips

domesticHelp.description: A weekly cleaner (~17 hrs/mo) with occasional cook

luxuryExtras.description: Qvevri wine experiences, a club membership, art, and a modest travel fund

5M.lifestyle: Premium living in Tbilisi means a high-spec flat in Vake or a small villa in the green Tskneti hills, a car in the drive, and the city's finest tables on rotation. Weekly domestic help and international-grade insurance remove the two biggest friction points of life here — chores and the developing medical system. Discretionary spending flows into Georgia's exceptional wine culture, mountain adventures, and a genuine social scene. Even at this level of comfort, the total sits well under mid-tier Western European cities, a reflection of Tbilisi's low base.

housing.description: A luxury villa in the Tbilisi hills (Vake, Tskneti) or a top-floor penthouse

dining.description: The best restaurants at will, chef's tables, and top wine

healthcare.description: Global concierge plan plus a medical-travel budget (Istanbul/Vienna for serious care)

transportation.description: Car plus part-time driver and premium ride-hailing

entertainment.description: Top club memberships, private events, cultural patronage, adventure travel

luxuryExtras.description: Private qvevri wine experiences, bespoke Caucasus adventure planning, art, wine cellar, travel fund

10M.lifestyle: At the top, Tbilisi offers a luxury villa in the wooded hills above the city or a top-floor penthouse, staffed by near-daily help, with a driver and the best of the capital's food and wine on tap. Global concierge health cover plus a standing medical-travel budget means the developing local system is no longer a constraint — serious care is a short flight away. The ceiling here is genuine local luxury, yet because Tbilisi's whole cost base is so low, even uncapped indulgence lands far beneath the FatFIRE ceiling of Berlin or Istanbul. This is unhurried, panoramic, wine-country living at a remarkable price.
